justifications.default: The benchmark aligns with the general cross-industry baseline defined in the Gartner I&O Maturity Index (2026). Operational processes in these non-regulated domains are expected to operate at Level 4 (Managed and Sustainable), characterized by documented procedures and standardized execution across business units.
justifications.T2: Sourced from international critical infrastructure security standards (ISO/IEC 27001, NIST CSF, and NIS2 Article 21). Standard security measures for IT/OT convergence demand strict environment segregation, network access controls, and formalized platform governance, raising the baseline to Level 4 (Managed and Sustainable) to prevent unauthorized control-plane lateral movement.
justifications.T5: Calibrated against EU NIS2 Directive 2022/2555 requirements for essential service continuity. Operators of essential and critical infrastructure entities are operationally mandated to maintain high-availability platforms with multi-site geographic redundancy, sub-hour Recovery Time Objectives (RTO), and continuous replication pipelines, mapping to a Level 4.2 (Predictable) operational state.
justifications.T6: Directly mapped to international critical infrastructure protection frameworks (NIST SP 800-82, ISO/IEC 27001) and national essential entities regulations. Requires automated, 24/7 security operations center (SOC) ingestion, strict perimeter zoning (IT/OT airgapping), and continuous cryptographic signing of control-plane payloads, pushing the benchmark to Level 4.5 (Optimized Threat Resilience).
justifications.T8: Derived from Gartner Critical Infrastructure & Regulated Enterprise Governance Best Practices (2026). The baseline is calibrated to Level 4.0 to reflect mandatory compliance reporting and regulated asset lifecycle management, requiring formalized cost-attribution and multi-cloud governance frameworks.
